summary: Comprehensive backend testing of Andromeda POS FastAPI app. 33/33 pytest tests passed across Auth, Menu, Tables, Customers, Inventory, Orders, and Reports. All resource endpoints correctly require Bearer JWT; order numbers monotonically increment from 1047; dine-in table side effects + customer order count increments + table freeing on completion all work; reports summary aggregates correctly with weeklySales (7 entries) and topItems (<=5).

minor.issue: No role gating — any authenticated staff (e.g., Driver) can create/update menu items, despite contracts.md stating 'Manager only'. require_role() exists in auth.py but is a no-op stub never used.

todaySales/ordersToday do not filter by current day — they sum ALL orders ever. Field name implies 'today'. Seeded fixture orders use mins_ago timestamps so it works initially, but it will accumulate forever as new orders are placed across days.
weeklySales is a hardcoded fallback array (`_WEEKLY_FALLBACK`) — never computed from orders. Acceptable for MVP per contracts.md, but not real data.
Requires >=5 digits (returns 400 below threshold). Acceptable, but the contract example uses an 11-digit string so callers should be aware.
Status string is not validated against an enum (any string accepted).
Order `type` and `payment` are free-form strings — no validation that type∈{dine-in,collection,delivery} or payment∈{cash,card,unpaid}.

action_items: (Optional) Enforce Manager role on POST/PUT menu endpoints if multi-role gating is desired.
(Optional) Filter reports.summary by today's date instead of summing all orders.
(Optional) Add Literal/Enum validation to Order.type, Order.payment, Table.status.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: `require_role()` is a no-op placeholder — either implement it or remove to avoid confusion.
server.py: `_next_order_number` uses ReturnDocument default; works because seed sets seq=1046 and $inc returns post-update doc — verified first new order = 1047 in tests.
server.py: `report_summary` should compute weeklySales from orders for real data, but is acceptable for MVP per contracts.md.
server.py is 409 lines — within limits, well organized; no DRY violations of note.
models.py: Order.type/status/payment + Table.status should use Literal types for type safety.
auth.py: bcrypt hashes generated correctly ($2b$ format) — verified via successful PIN login.
db.py: Mongo `_id` correctly excluded via PROJECTION={'_id':0} on all reads. counters collection uses string `_id`='order_number' which is fine.
test_credentials: Manager PIN 1234 → user s1 (Sarah Mitchell). Cashier 2345/3456, Driver 4567 (verified via seed).
seed_data_creation: Tests created TEST_-prefixed customer + TEST_Side menu item + TEST_Walk-in orders. Customer is deleted in test; menu item and TEST orders persist but use TEST_ prefix and unique IDs so are easily identifiable. cu1 'Emma Wilson' orders count was incremented once by the create-order test (from 23 to 24).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 33 backend tests pass. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_andromeda_api.py is the regression suite — re-run with: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. Order counter increments on every test run (~2 orders/run), so order numbers will keep climbing — this is expected and verifies monotonicity. Some seeded customers (cu1) have their orders count incremented per run. Frontend testing was explicitly skipped per request.
